mcqs.learning_point: Identify the different angles formed by three intersecting lines
mcqs.question: Three distinct straight lines intersect at a single point O. How many different angles are formed at O?
mcqs.explanation: When three lines cross at one point, each line creates two opposite rays. The six rays form six angles around the point (each pair of adjacent rays makes an angle). Some students think only four angles are formed, but the correct count is six.

mcqs.learning_point: Trace relationships among angles in a diagram
mcqs.question: In a diagram, three lines intersect at point O, forming six angles labeled consecutively as ∠AOB, ∠BOC, ∠COD, ∠DOE, ∠EOF, and ∠FOA. If ∠AOB measures 40°, what is the measure of ∠COD?
mcqs.explanation: ∠AOB and ∠COD are vertically opposite angles because they are formed by the same two intersecting lines and lie opposite each other. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so ∠COD also measures 40°. The other options are unrelated to this relationship.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of angles are vertically opposite angles when three lines intersect at a point?
mcqs.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are formed by two intersecting lines and lie opposite each other. In the three‑line configuration, ∠AOB and ∠COD are opposite each other across the intersection, making them a pair of vertical angles. The other pairs share a common side and are adjacent, not vertical.

mcqs.question: In the same configuration of three intersecting lines, if ∠AOB = 70°, which angle is supplementary to ∠AOB?
mcqs.explanation: Angles that share a common side and together form a straight line are supplementary; they add up to 180°. ∠AOB and the adjacent angle ∠BOC lie on a straight line, so they are supplementary (70° + 110° = 180°). ∠FOA is also adjacent but on the opposite side; either could be correct, but the standard convention takes the next clockwise angle, which is ∠BOC. The other options are not adjacent to ∠AOB and therefore are not supplementary.
